title: Denmark, Greenland Confirm Security Deal, Stress Sovereignty Untouched Amid Public Skepticism
detail: Denmark and Greenland confirmed on September 19, 2026 that they had reached the security agreement Trump described a day earlier, while pushing back on his framing that it hands Washington 'permanent control.' Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the pact 'recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity' of the Kingdom of Denmark and the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination, calling it 'great for NATO and Europe' because it 'strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic Area.' Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said 'a long period of uncertainty will hopefully be replaced by a binding agreement,' and Greenland's Foreign Minister Múte B. Egede said 'I'm pleased that we finally have an end product within reach. It's about time' — the deal is due to be signed at the UN General Assembly in New York the following week, pending Danish parliamentary approval. NATO Defense College analyst Richard Weitz said the agreement 'defuses perhaps one of the most severe sources of internal tension' within the alliance, while Danish Institute for International Studies researcher Mikkel Olesen and Arctic security expert Marc Jacobsen cautioned the concessions were narrower than Trump's rhetoric suggested, since Denmark and Greenland had never wanted Russian or Chinese bases on the island. Greenlanders themselves reacted with what the Philadelphia Inquirer described as nervousness and skepticism, citing a lack of transparency over cost, troop numbers and whether Greenlandic representatives were fully at the table during months of closed-door negotiations.
